definition_zh: 到期；失效；期满结束；去世；呼气
definition_en: to reach the end of the period for which a document, ticket, or agreement is valid, to come to an end, or, in literary use, to die
core_image: 一张证件上的日期被红笔圈住，过了那天它就自动作废
scene: 护照上的日期眼看就要到了，他得赶在出发前换一本新的。My passport expires next month, so I must renew it before the trip.
sceneCN: 这里 expire 是「到期」（第 1 个义项：证件上写明的有效期走到尽头）；句意：我的护照下个月到期，所以我必须在出行前换新的。

pos.zh: 到期；失效；期满结束；去世；呼气

derivatives.zh: 由动词 expire 加名词词尾 -y 构成，义为「到期；有效期」
由 expire 加 -ation 构成，义为「期满；截止」，多见于美式英语
由 expire 加 -ory 构成，义为「呼气的」，用于医学与生理学

senses.title: To reach the end of its validity
senses.definition: of a passport, visa, or similar document, to reach the last date on which it can legally be used
senses.definitionCN: 护照、签证等证件走到可以合法使用的最后日期
senses.example: My passport expires next month.
senses.exampleCN: 我的护照下个月到期。
senses.why: The Latin verb first meant to breathe out the last breath, so the ending of a fixed term is felt as a small death.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词本指呼出最后一口气，因此一个固定期限的结束被感受为一次小小的死亡。

senses.title: To stop being usable
senses.definition: of a ticket, an offer, or a right, to stop being usable because the time limit has passed
senses.definitionCN: 票据、优惠或权利因期限已过而不再可用
senses.example: The return ticket expires in three days.
senses.exampleCN: 这张回程票三天后失效。
senses.why: Once the time limit runs out the object keeps its shape but loses its power, which is the everyday sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 期限一过，票据的外形还在，效力却没了，这正是这个词最日常的一层意义。

senses.title: To come to the end of a term
senses.definition: of a period, a lease, or a term of office, to come to an end
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间、租约或任期走到尽头
senses.example: The lease expires at the end of June.
senses.exampleCN: 租约在六月底到期。
senses.why: Any fixed span of time has a last moment, so the word extends from paper documents to time itself.
senses.whyCN: 任何一段固定时间都有一个最后的时刻，于是这个词从纸质文件扩展到时间本身。

senses.title: To die
senses.definition: to die, used as a gentle or literary word
senses.definitionCN: 去世，用作委婉或书面说法
senses.example: The old poet expired quietly at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老诗人在黎明时安静地离世。
senses.why: Breathing out the last breath is the oldest image of dying, and the euphemism has survived in literary English.
senses.whyCN: 呼出最后一口气是关于死亡最古老的意象，这一委婉说法在书面英语中保留至今。

senses.title: To breathe out
senses.definition: to breathe air out of the lungs, used in medical and formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 把气从肺里呼出，用于医学和正式文字
senses.example: The patient was asked to expire slowly through the mouth.
senses.exampleCN: 医生请病人用嘴慢慢呼气。
senses.why: The technical sense returns to the plain Latin meaning of breathing out, without the idea of death.
senses.whyCN: 这一技术义项回到拉丁语最朴素的意思「往外呼气」，不带死亡意味。

intro.en: Expire comes from Latin exspirare, to breathe out, and by extension to breathe out the last breath and die; English also uses it for the ending of a fixed term.
intro.cn: expire 来自拉丁语 exspirare（向外呼气），引申为「呼出最后一口气而死」；英语又用它表示固定期限的结束。

items.en: Spirare means to breathe, and the prefix ex- means out.
items.cn: spirare 意为呼吸，前缀 ex- 表示向外。

items.en: Exspirare means to breathe out, and also to breathe out the last breath, that is, to die.
items.cn: exspirare 意为呼出，也指呼出最后一口气，即死亡。

items.en: The same verb is used for a period of time running out.
items.cn: 同一个动词也用于表示一段时间走完。

items.en: Espirer carries the word into French with the sense of coming to an end.
items.cn: espirer 把这个词带入法语，含「走到尽头」之意。

items.en: Expire appears in English in the fifteenth century, first for dying and then for documents ending.
items.cn: expire 在十五世纪进入英语，先指死亡，后指文件的期限结束。

items.en: Modern English makes the document sense dominant and keeps the sense of dying as literary.
items.cn: 现代英语让「证件到期」成为主要义项，而「去世」保留为书面语。

note.en: Expire belongs to the spirare family of breathing words, and it also sits close to ordinary words for ending.
note.cn: expire 属于 spirare 这一「呼吸」词族，同时也靠近一批表示「结束」的普通词。

normalIntro.en: Expire joins ex-, out, to spirare, to breathe: something breathes out its last and then stops.
normalIntro.cn: expire 由 ex-（向外）与 spirare（呼吸）组成：某物呼出最后一口气，然后停下。

normal.en: A passport or a visa expires on a printed date.
normal.cn: 护照或签证在印好的日期到期。

normal.en: A ticket that has expired cannot be used.
normal.cn: 过期的票不能再用。

normal.en: A lease expires when its term runs out.
normal.cn: 租约在期限用尽时到期。

normal.en: In older writing, to expire is simply to die.
normal.cn: 在较旧的文字里，expire 就是「去世」。

normal.en: Compare expire with end: expire adds the idea of a fixed limit that has been reached.
normal.cn: 对比 end：expire 多了「走到既定界限」这一层意思。

abstract.en: Picture a passport page where the printed date slowly fades.
abstract.cn: 想象护照内页上那个印刷日期慢慢淡去。

abstract.en: Think of a ticket that goes grey and blank the moment the clock strikes twelve.
abstract.cn: 想象一张票在钟敲十二下的那一刻变灰、变空白。

abstract.en: Imagine a calendar page tearing itself off on the last day of a lease.
abstract.cn: 想象租约的最后一天，日历自己撕下一页。

examples.en: My passport expires next month, so I have booked an appointment to renew it.
examples.cn: 我的护照下个月到期，所以我已经预约了换发。

examples.en: The discount code expired at midnight, and the price went back up.
examples.cn: 折扣码在午夜失效，价格又涨了回去。

examples.en: The old fisherman expired in his sleep at the age of ninety.
examples.cn: 那位老渔夫在九十岁时于睡梦中离世。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一克斯派尔」——谐音近似「一刻死派尔」：一刻之间气就断了，于是既指「到期」，也指「去世」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）+ spirare（呼吸）→ exspirare（呼出；断气；期限走完）→ 古法语 espirer → 英语 expire，核心义是「把最后一口气呼出去」。

sensesIntro.en: Expire starts from paper that has a printed last date, widens to any fixed term that runs out, and keeps the old sense of dying as a literary echo.
sensesIntro.cn: expire 从印着最后日期的证件出发，扩展到任何走完的固定期限，并以书面语的形式保留「去世」这一古老义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dated card that quietly stops working once the red circle is passed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张印着日期的卡片，红圈一过就悄悄失效。

branches.en: A document reaching its printed final date is the core modern sense.
branches.cn: 证件走到印好的最后日期，是现代最核心的义项。

branches.en: Losing force after the time limit is the practical sense for tickets and offers.
branches.cn: 过了期限就失去效力，是票据与优惠层面的实用义项。

branches.en: A term or a lease ending extends the image from paper to time.
branches.cn: 任期或租约结束，把意象从纸面扩展到时间。

branches.en: The literary sense of dying keeps the old image of the last breath.
branches.cn: 书面语中「去世」的义项保留了「最后一口气」的古老意象。

branches.en: Both breathing out and dying come straight from the Latin verb.
branches.cn: 「呼气」与「去世」都直接来自那个拉丁语动词。

intro.en: Expire is built from the Latin prefix ex- and the root spirare, and English has added several related forms around it.
intro.cn: expire 由拉丁语前缀 ex- 与词根 spirare 构成，英语围绕它又造出了若干同族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin spirare means to breathe; with ex- it becomes exspirare, to breathe out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spirare 意为呼吸，加上 ex- 成为 exspirare，意为呼出。

items.example: The prefix ex- turns breathing into breathing out.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 把「呼吸」变成「向外呼出」。

items.example: Spirare is the root of spirit and of expire.
items.exampleCN: spirare 是 spirit 与 expire 共同的词根。

items.example: Exspirare joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: exspirare 把前缀与词根合在一起。

items.meaning: to come to the end of a period of validity
items.example: Passports expire on a printed date.
items.exampleCN: 护照在印好的日期到期。

items.meaning: the end of a period of validity
items.example: The expiry date is printed on the box.
items.exampleCN: 到期日印在盒子上。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms expiration.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 expiration。

items.meaning: the ending of a valid period
items.example: Expiration is the more formal twin of expiry.
items.exampleCN: expiration 是 expiry 更正式的对应形式。

items.example: The suffix -ory forms expiratory.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ory 构成 expiratory。

items.example: Expiratory describes the outward breath.
items.exampleCN: expiratory 描述向外呼气的过程。

definition_zh: 到期；期满；有效期；到期日；去世
definition_en: the end of a period during which something is valid, the period itself, the date on which it ends, or, in literary use, death
core_image: 牛奶盒侧面印着一行小字，标出它还能喝到哪一天
scene: 牛奶盒上的日期已经过去两天，她只好把它倒掉。The milk is two days past its expiry date, so she poured it away.
sceneCN: 这里 expiry 是「到期日」（第 3 个义项：印在包装上的失效日期）；句意：这盒牛奶已经过了保质期两天，所以她把它倒掉了。

pos.zh: 到期；期满；有效期；到期日；去世

derivatives.zh: expiry 的动词形式，义为「到期；失效」，名词即由它加 -y 构成

senses.title: The end of a valid period
senses.definition: the fact of a period of validity coming to an end
senses.definitionCN: 一段有效期限走到尽头这一事实
senses.example: The expiry of her visa forced her to leave the country.
senses.exampleCN: 签证到期迫使她离开这个国家。
senses.why: The noun simply names the moment when the Latin verb has finished breathing out its term.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词只是给「那个拉丁语动词把期限呼尽」的那一刻命名。

senses.title: The period of validity
senses.definition: the length of time for which something can be used
senses.definitionCN: 某物可以使用的时长
senses.example: A short expiry keeps the medicine safe to use.
senses.exampleCN: 较短的有效期让药品用起来更安全。
senses.why: If the ending is a point, the stretch before it can be named with the same word, a common shift in English nouns.
senses.whyCN: 既然终点是一个点，终点之前的那段时间也可以用同一个词来指，这是英语名词常见的转指。

senses.title: The printed date
senses.definition: the date printed on a product or a document after which it should not be used
senses.definitionCN: 印在产品或文件上、过了就不该再用的日期
senses.example: Please check the expiry date on the carton before you buy it.
senses.exampleCN: 买之前请看一下纸盒上的到期日。
senses.why: Shops need a concrete date on the pack, so the abstract end becomes a printed number.
senses.whyCN: 商店需要包装上一个具体的日期，于是抽象的终点变成了一串印出来的数字。

senses.title: Death
senses.definition: death, used in formal or literary writing
senses.definitionCN: 死亡，用于正式或书面文字
senses.example: The expiry of the old king left the country without an heir.
senses.exampleCN: 老国王的去世让这个国家失去了继承人。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the root is the last breath, so the noun can still name a death in solemn prose.
senses.whyCN: 这个词根最古老的意义是最后一口气，所以这个名词在庄重的文字里仍可指死亡。

intro.en: Expiry is an English formation from the verb expire plus the noun suffix -y, first recorded in the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: expiry 是英语本土构成的词，由动词 expire 加名词词尾 -y 组成，最早见于十八世纪。

items.en: Spirare, to breathe, is the root shared with expire.
items.cn: spirare（呼吸）是与 expire 共有的词根。

items.en: Exspirare adds out and covers both breathing out and dying.
items.cn: exspirare 加上「向外」，兼指呼出与断气。

items.en: Expire enters English as a verb meaning to come to an end.
items.cn: expire 作为动词进入英语，意为走到尽头。

items.en: The noun expiry is formed from the verb with -y.
items.cn: 名词 expiry 由这个动词加 -y 构成。

items.en: British shops and labels use expiry date where American English prefers expiration date.
items.cn: 英国商店与标签用 expiry date，而美式英语更常用 expiration date。

items.en: Modern dictionaries also record a literary sense, death.
items.cn: 现代词典还收录了「死亡」这一书面语义项。

note.en: Expiry is the noun of expire, and it also stands beside ordinary words for a deadline.
note.cn: expiry 是 expire 的名词形式，同时也与表示「最后期限」的普通词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Expiry is expire turned into a noun, so it names the date, the period, or the ending itself.
normalIntro.cn: expiry 是 expire 加 -y 变成的名词，因此它既能指到期日，也能指有效期，还能指到期这件事本身。

normal.en: The expiry date tells you when to stop using a product.
normal.cn: expiry date 告诉你什么时候该停止使用一件产品。

normal.en: British labels say expiry date; American labels often say expiration date.
normal.cn: 英国标签写 expiry date，美国标签常写 expiration date。

normal.en: The expiry of a visa is a date you must not miss.
normal.cn: 签证的到期日是一个绝不能错过的日子。

normal.en: An expiry notice reminds a customer to renew.
normal.cn: 到期通知提醒顾客续订。

normal.en: Compare expiry with deadline: a deadline is a limit for doing something, while an expiry is the end of validity.
normal.cn: 对比 expiry 与 deadline：deadline 是做某事的最后期限，expiry 则是有效期的终点。

abstract.en: Think of a ticket that tears itself in half at midnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一张票在午夜自己撕成两半。

abstract.en: Picture an oil lamp with a measured supply that burns steadily until it runs dry.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏油灯，油量是量好的，一直稳稳地烧到油尽。

abstract.en: Picture the small print on a milk carton, rubbed thin by the fridge shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象牛奶盒上的小字，被冰箱搁板磨得发淡。

examples.en: The expiry date on the carton has been rubbed off.
examples.cn: 纸盒上的到期日已经磨掉了。

examples.en: He left the country a week before the expiry of his work permit.
examples.cn: 他在工作许可到期前一周离开了这个国家。

examples.en: Milk is cheap here because it is close to its expiry.
examples.cn: 这里的牛奶便宜，因为快到保质期了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一克斯派尔瑞」——谐音近似「一刻死派尔」，一口气断掉的那天就是「到期日」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）+ spirare（呼吸）→ exspirare（呼出；断气）→ 英语动词 expire → 再加名词词尾 -y 构成 expiry，核心义是「有效期走到尽头的那一刻」。

sensesIntro.en: The noun moves from the ending itself to the period before it, then to the printed date, and finally to the old literary sense of death.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词从「到期」这件事本身，转到它之前的那段时间，再到印出来的日期，最后落到书面语中「死亡」的古老义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a printed date on a carton that marks the last safe day.
core.cn: 核心意象：包装上印着的一个日期，标出最后一个安全的日子。

branches.en: The ending itself is the most general sense of the noun.
branches.cn: 到期这件事本身，是这个名词最概括的义项。

branches.en: The stretch of time before the ending is named by the same noun.
branches.cn: 终点之前的那段时间，也用同一个名词来指。

branches.en: The date on the pack turns the abstract end into something you can read.
branches.cn: 包装上的日期把抽象的终点变成可以读到的东西。

branches.en: The literary sense of death comes from the old image of the last breath.
branches.cn: 书面语中「死亡」的义项，来自「最后一口气」的古老意象。

branches.en: Both the ending and the printed date are what a shopper checks in a shop.
branches.cn: 到期这件事与印出的日期，都是顾客在店里会查看的内容。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词根是 spirare（呼吸），它同时给出 expire 与 expiration。

definition_zh: 解释；说明；阐明
definition_en: to make something clear; to give a reason for something; to account for a decision or action
core_image: 把褶皱的东西摊平，让人一眼看清
scene: 老师耐心地解释了这条语法规则。 The teacher patiently explained the grammar rule.
sceneCN: 这里 explain 是「解释」（第 1 个义项）；句意：老师耐心地解释了这条语法规则。

senses.title: Make clear
senses.definition: to make something clear or easy to understand
senses.definitionCN: 使某事清楚、容易理解
senses.example: Could you explain the rule again?
senses.exampleCN: 你能再解释一遍这条规则吗？
senses.why: The core sense is making something flat and clear.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是把事情摊平、讲清楚。

senses.title: Give a reason
senses.definition: to give a reason for something
senses.definitionCN: 为某事给出原因
senses.example: He explained why he was late.
senses.exampleCN: 他解释了自己迟到的原因。
senses.why: Making clear includes showing the cause.
senses.whyCN: 讲清楚也包括说明原因。

senses.title: Account for
senses.definition: to account for a decision or defend an action
senses.definitionCN: 说明某项决定的理由或为行为辩解
senses.example: She explained her decision to the board.
senses.exampleCN: 她向董事会说明了她的决定。
senses.why: Explaining becomes answering for a choice.
senses.whyCN: 解释变成为自己的选择作交代。

intro.en: Explain comes from Latin explanare, to make flat and clear.
intro.cn: explain 源自拉丁语 explanare，意为「摊平、使清楚」。

items.en: Planus means flat or clear.
items.cn: planus 意为平坦、清楚。

items.en: Explanare means to flatten out.
items.cn: explanare 意为把东西摊平。

items.en: Explainer keeps the sense of unfolding.
items.cn: explainer 保留「展开」的含义。

items.en: Explanen means to make plain.
items.cn: explinen 意为使明白。

items.en: Explain adds the sense of giving reasons.
items.cn: explain 增加了「说明原因」之义。

items.en: Explain yourself means to justify your action.
items.cn: explain yourself 意为为自己的行为辩解。

branches.en: Meaning and cause are both made plain.

definition_zh: 明确的；清楚的；直言的；露骨的；显式的
definition_en: stated clearly and in detail, leaving nothing to be inferred or guessed
core_image: 折起的纸被完全摊平，每一道折痕都露出来
scene: 监考老师指着黑板上的规则说： The instructions are explicit: no phones in the exam room.
sceneCN: 这里 explicit 是「明确写明的」（第 1 个义项：完全说清、不留暗示）；句意：规则写得很明确：考场内不许用手机。图中可辨识物件：黑板、规则清单、手机收纳盒、监考老师。

pos.zh: 明确的；清楚的；直言的；露骨的

senses.title: Fully stated: nothing left implied
senses.titleCN: 明确写出：不留任何暗示
senses.definition: expressed in clear and complete words, with nothing left for the reader to infer
senses.definitionCN: 用清楚完整的话表达，不给读者留下需要推断的空白
senses.example: The instructions are explicit: no phones in the exam room.
senses.exampleCN: 规则写得很明确：考场内不许用手机。
senses.why: Latin explicare is ex 'out' + plicare 'to fold'. Explicit is the sheet unfolded: every line that could have stayed hidden is now open to view.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 explicare 是 ex「出」+ plicare「折叠」。explicit 就是被展开的那张纸：原本可以藏住的每一行，现在都摊在外面。

senses.title: Precise and unambiguous
senses.titleCN: 确切无歧义：不给第二种读法
senses.definition: so clearly worded that it can be understood in only one way
senses.definitionCN: 措辞清楚到只有一种理解方式
senses.example: The doctor gave an explicit warning about mixing the drugs.
senses.exampleCN: 医生对混用这些药物发出了明确警告。
senses.why: A folded page hides parts of the text. An explicit wording lays the whole sentence flat, so there is no fold left in which a second meaning could hide.
senses.whyCN: 折起的页面会遮住部分文字。明确的措辞把整句话摊平，于是没有一道折痕还能藏住第二种意思。

senses.title: Open about something usually hidden
senses.titleCN: 直言不讳：把通常藏着的话说出来
senses.definition: willing to state something openly that people often leave unsaid
senses.definitionCN: 愿意公开说出人们通常避而不谈的事
senses.example: She was explicit about her reasons for leaving.
senses.exampleCN: 她直言不讳地说明了自己离开的原因。
senses.why: The verb can be reflexive: a person unfolds his own motives instead of leaving them folded inside. Openness is the human version of the same image.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以指向人自身：一个人把自己的动机展开，而不是折起来藏在里面。坦率就是同一意象在人的身上的版本。

senses.title: Sexually explicit content
senses.titleCN: 露骨性内容：不加遮掩地呈现
senses.definition: showing sexual acts or nudity in an open, detailed way
senses.definitionCN: 以公开、详细的方式呈现性行为或裸体
senses.example: The film is rated for explicit content.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影因含露骨内容而被分级。
senses.why: The modern phrase uses 'explicit' for what is shown rather than implied. Nothing is folded away or concealed, and that is exactly why the label warns.
senses.whyCN: 现代短语用 explicit 指“直接呈现而非暗示”的内容。没有什么被折起或遮住，这正是这个标签要警告的地方。

senses.title: Explicit language: open swearing
senses.titleCN: 粗口直出：不加消音的歌词或言语
senses.definition: containing swear words or crude language that is not edited out
senses.definitionCN: 含有未消音、未删改的粗话或脏话
senses.example: The album carries an explicit lyrics warning.
senses.exampleCN: 这张专辑带有“含粗口歌词”的警示。
senses.why: A clean version folds the offensive word away; an explicit version leaves it unfolded in the open. The same contrast between hidden and displayed.
senses.whyCN: 干净版把冒犯性的词折起来藏掉；explicit 版则让它展开在外。仍是“藏”与“露”的同一组对立。

senses.title: Explicit formula: fully specified
senses.titleCN: 显式公式：每一项都写出来
senses.definition: in mathematics and logic, stated in full form rather than left in shorthand or implication
senses.definitionCN: 数学与逻辑中，以完整形式写出，而不是用简写或隐含
senses.example: The paper gives an explicit formula for the solution.
senses.exampleCN: 论文给出了解的显式公式。
senses.why: A formula in shorthand is folded up; an explicit formula multiplies it out so that every term stands visible. This is the algebraic version of unfolding.
senses.whyCN: 简写公式是折起来的；显式公式把它乘开，让每一项都立在外面。这是“展开”的代数版本。

senses.title: Explicit consent: permission in plain terms
senses.titleCN: 明确同意：法律与医疗上的明示许可
senses.definition: clear, recorded permission given for a specific act, especially in law or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 对某一具体行为给出的清楚、有记录的许可，尤用于法律或医疗
senses.example: The study required explicit consent from every participant.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究要求每位参与者明确同意。
senses.why: Consent that is merely implied can be disputed later. Explicit consent is written out and signed, so the permission cannot be folded back into silence.
senses.whyCN: 仅仅隐含的同意日后可能有争议。explicit consent 被写出来并签署，许可就无法再折回沉默里。

senses.title: Explicit memory: consciously available
senses.titleCN: 外显记忆：能清楚说出来的记忆
senses.definition: in psychology, a memory that a person can consciously recall and state
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中指人能有意识地回忆并说出的记忆
senses.example: Explicit memory lets you recall your first day at school.
senses.exampleCN: 外显记忆让你能回想起上学第一天。
senses.why: What is explicit is laid out where the mind can look at it. Explicit memory is knowledge a person can unfold and describe, unlike a skill that stays folded into the body.
senses.whyCN: explicit 的东西被铺在心灵能看见的地方。外显记忆是人能展开并描述的知识，不同于折进身体里的技能。

senses.title: The old manuscript explicit: here the book ends
senses.titleCN: 古抄本收尾语：书到此展开完毕
senses.definition: historical, noun: the closing word or note of a medieval manuscript, marking the end of the text
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法，名词：中世纪抄本末尾的收尾词或题记，标记正文结束
senses.example: The scribe wrote explicit at the foot of the last page.
senses.exampleCN: 抄写员在最后一页末尾写下了 explicit。
senses.why: Medieval scribes ended with explicitus est liber, 'the book is unfolded/read out'. The word that marked a completed reading became the label for the end itself.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪抄写员用 explicitus est liber 收尾，意为“书已展开／读完了”。标记“读完”的词，最后变成了“结尾”本身的标签。

intro.en: Explicit comes from Latin explicare 'to unfold, unravel, explain', ex- 'out' + plicare 'to fold'. The English adjective, meaning 'clear, not ambiguous', is first recorded in the 1610s through French explicite.
intro.cn: explicit 来自拉丁语 explicare“展开、解开、解释”，由 ex-“出”+ plicare“折叠”构成。英语形容词“清楚、不含糊”于 1610 年代经法语 explicite 进入英语。

items.en: Explicare meant 'to unfold, unroll; disentangle; explain'. The image is physical: a folded thing is opened until its parts can be seen.
items.cn: explicare 意为“展开、铺开；解开；解释”。意象是物理的：把折起的东西打开，直到各部分都能看见。

items.en: Plicare 'to fold' goes back to PIE *plek- 'to plait, weave, fold'. The same root gives plait, plexus, complex, and the two Latin directions in- and ex-.
items.cn: plicare“折叠”可追溯到原始印欧语 *plek-“编织、折叠”。同一词根生出 plait、plexus、complex，以及拉丁语里 in- 与 ex- 两个方向。

items.en: Explicitus, a variant past participle of explicare, meant 'unobstructed, clear'. What is unfolded is also unblocked: nothing is left in the way of understanding.
items.cn: explicitus 是 explicare 的异体过去分词，意为“无阻碍的、清楚的”。被展开的东西也畅通无阻：理解的道路上没有东西挡着。

items.en: English takes the adjective from French explicite with the sense 'clear, plain, not ambiguous'. It is the opposite of implicit, which is folded in.
items.cn: 英语从法语 explicite 借入形容词，义为“清楚的、明白的、不含糊的”。它是 implicit 的反面，后者是“折进去的”。

items.en: Scribes closed a manuscript with explicitus est liber, 'the book is unfolded / read out'. From that formula, explicit became the word written at the end of a text.
items.cn: 抄写员用 explicitus est liber“书已展开／读完了”来结束抄本。从这个固定语开始，explicit 成了写在文本末尾的那个词。

items.en: Modern English keeps the 'nothing hidden' core: explicit instructions, explicit consent, sexually explicit, explicit memory. Its mirror is implicit, in- 'in' + plicare 'fold'.
items.cn: 现代英语保留“没有隐藏”的内核：explicit instructions、explicit consent、sexually explicit、explicit memory。它的镜像是 implicit，即 in-“内”+ plicare“折”。

note.en: The first group is close in spelling or word parts; the second is close in meaning. Form first, then sense.
note.cn: 第一组在拼写或构词成分上接近；第二组在词义上接近。先看词形，再看意义。

entries.definition: implied but not stated. In- 'in' + plicare 'fold' means folded in, the mirror image of explicit's unfolded.
entries.definitionCN: 隐含而未明说的。in-“内”+ plicare“折”意为折进去，正是 explicit“展开”的镜像。

entries.definition: to explain a text or idea in detail. It is the verb; explicit is the adjective for what has been fully laid out.
entries.definitionCN: 详细解释文本或观点。它是动词；explicit 是形容词，形容已被完全铺开的内容。

entries.definition: to use something for profit, or a bold deed. It comes from Latin explicitum 'something unfolded or settled', but its meaning moved to 'turn to account'.
entries.definitionCN: 利用；开发；也可指功绩。它来自拉丁语 explicitum“被展开或了结之事”，但词义转向“加以利用”。

entries.definition: easy to understand or see. Clear can describe a style or a view; explicit stresses that the content is actually stated, not merely easy.
entries.definitionCN: 易懂的；清晰的。clear 可形容文风或视野；explicit 强调内容确实被说出来，而不只是容易懂。

entries.definition: fixed, certain, and not likely to change. Definite stresses certainty; explicit stresses complete expression.
entries.definitionCN: 确定的；不会改变的。definite 强调确定性；explicit 强调表达完整。

entries.definition: having only one possible meaning. It focuses on the absence of ambiguity; explicit focuses on the presence of full statement.
entries.definitionCN: 只有一种可能含义的。它聚焦于“没有歧义”；explicit 聚焦于“把话完整说出来”。

entries.definition: stated openly and specifically, especially in a contract or law. Express is formal and legal; explicit is broader and also covers sexual content.
entries.definitionCN: 明示的，尤用于合同或法律。express 正式且偏法律；explicit 范围更广，也可指露骨内容。

normalIntro.en: Real parts, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 真实的构词成分、真实短语和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ex- 'out' + plicare 'fold' = unfold. Explicit is the sheet opened flat, with every fold laid out.
normal.cn: ex-“出”+ plicare“折”= 展开。explicit 就是被摊平的那张纸，每一道折痕都铺开。

normal.en: The same plicare gives implicit 'folded in', implicate, explicate, complexity and plait.
normal.cn: 同一个 plicare 生出 implicit“折进去”、implicate、explicate、complexity 和 plait。

normal.en: Medieval scribes ended with explicitus est liber, 'the book is unfolded / read out'; from this the word explicit came to mark the end of a text.
normal.cn: 中世纪抄写员用 explicitus est liber“书已展开／读完了”收尾；由此 explicit 成了标记文本结尾的词。

normal.en: To make something explicit is the everyday phrase for bringing an unstated rule or feeling into the open.
normal.cn: make something explicit 是日常短语，意为把没说出口的规则或感受摆到明面上。

normal.en: Do not confuse explicit with exhibit: exhibit has habere 'hold' and means hold out; explicit has plicare 'fold' and means unfold.
normal.cn: 不要把 explicit 和 exhibit 混淆：exhibit 的词根是 habere“握”，意为举出去；explicit 的词根是 plicare“折”，意为展开。

abstract.en: A letter folded small: implicit keeps it closed, explicit opens it flat and reads every line aloud.
abstract.cn: 一封折得很小的信：implicit 让它保持合着，explicit 把它摊平，并逐行读出来。

abstract.en: A rule everyone follows but nobody says is implicit; writing it on the door makes it explicit.
abstract.cn: 一条人人都遵守却没人说出口的规则是 implicit；把它写在门上，就变成 explicit。

abstract.en: Every fold has an inside and an outside. Implicit is the inside; explicit is the outside turned toward the reader.
abstract.cn: 每道折痕都有里面和外面。implicit 是里面；explicit 是翻向读者的外面。

examples.en: The instructions were explicit: no phones in the exam room.
examples.cn: 规则写得很明确：考场内不许用手机。

examples.en: She was explicit about her reasons for leaving.
examples.cn: 她直言不讳地说明了自己离开的原因。

examples.en: The film is rated for explicit content.
examples.cn: 这部电影因含露骨内容而被分级。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一克斯普利说」——把折起的话全铺开、普利落落地说明白 → explicit 明确的

root: 源自拉丁语 explicitus「无阻碍的、清楚的」，是 explicare「展开、解开、解释」的异体过去分词，由 ex「出」+ plicare「折叠」构成。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of explicit share one gesture: a folded surface is opened until nothing is hidden — a rule, a warning, a motive, a sexual scene, a swear word, a formula, a consent form, a memory, or the end of a manuscript.
sensesIntro.cn: explicit 的九个义项共享同一个动作：把折起的表面打开，直到没有东西被遮住——规则、警告、动机、性场景、脏话、公式、同意书、记忆，或一部抄本的结尾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded sheet is opened flat so that every line can be read.
core.cn: 核心意象：折起的纸被完全摊平，每一行都能读到。

branches.en: THE OPEN PAGE: a fully stated instruction or warning leaves no second reading.
branches.cn: 摊开的页面：完整写出的指示或警告，不留下第二种读法。

branches.en: OPENNESS ABOUT THE HIDDEN: a motive, a sexual scene, or a swear word is brought out instead of folded away.
branches.cn: 对隐藏之事的坦白：动机、性场景或脏话被摆出来，而不是折起来藏掉。

branches.en: THE FULLY SPECIFIED: an explicit formula writes out every term, and explicit memory can be recalled and stated.
branches.cn: 完整写明：显式公式写出每一项，外显记忆能被回忆并说出。

branches.en: THE SIGNED PERMISSION: explicit consent cannot be folded back into silence.
branches.cn: 签署的许可：明确同意无法再折回沉默里。

branches.en: THE OLD COLOPHON: explicitus est liber marked the book as unfolded and finished.
branches.cn: 古老的收尾语：explicitus est liber 标记书已展开、已读完。

intro.en: Explicit is the adjective from Latin explicare: ex- 'out' plus the plic- stem 'fold'. English builds adverbs, nouns, verbs and negatives on this stem, and the same root runs through implicit, complex and plait.
intro.cn: explicit 是拉丁语 explicare 的形容词：ex-“出”加 plic- 词干“折”。英语在这个词干上构成副词、名词、动词和否定形式；同一词根也贯穿 implicit、complex 和 plait。

latinIntro.en: Latin plicare 'to fold' has the compound explicare 'to unfold, explain' and its participle explicitus; the opposite compound implicare 'to fold in' gives implicit and implicate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 plicare“折叠”有复合形式 explicare“展开、解释”及其分词 explicitus；反方向的复合形式 implicare“折进去”生出 implicit 和 implicate。

items.meaningCN: 展开的；清楚的；明确写出的（ex- 出 + plicare 折）
items.example: The rule is explicit.
items.exampleCN: 规则很明确。

items.meaning: in a clear, fully stated way
items.meaningCN: 明确地；直截了当地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She explicitly denied the claim.
items.exampleCN: 她明确否认了这一说法。

items.meaningCN: 明确性；直白程度（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The explicitness of the warning left no doubt.
items.exampleCN: 警告的明确程度让人毫无怀疑。

items.meaning: to unfold the meaning of a text or idea
items.meaningCN: 解释；阐发（把折叠的含义展开）
items.example: The essay explicates the poem line by line.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章逐行阐释这首诗。

items.meaningCN: 解释；阐释（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: Her explication of the theory was clear.
items.exampleCN: 她对这个理论的阐释很清楚。

items.example: The error is explicable.
items.exampleCN: 这个错误是可以解释的。

items.meaningCN: 无法解释的（in- 表否定 + 可解释的）
items.example: The lights failed for inexplicable reasons.
items.exampleCN: 灯以无法解释的原因熄灭了。

items.meaning: folded in; suggested but not stated
items.meaningCN: 折进去的；隐含的（与 explicit 的“展开”相对）
items.example: There was an implicit threat in his tone.
items.exampleCN: 他的语气里有一种隐含的威胁。

items.meaning: to fold someone into a matter; to involve
items.meaningCN: 牵连；使卷入（把某人折进事件里）
items.example: The letter implicated two officials.
items.exampleCN: 这封信牵连了两名官员。

items.meaning: to turn something to use; a bold act

definition_zh: 开发利用；资源开采；商业开发；剥削；利用；漏洞利用
definition_en: the act of using a resource, situation or person for profit or advantage, whether fairly and productively or unfairly and at their expense
core_image: 一座山被层层剥开，矿石装上卡车运走，山脚下的人只拿到很少的报酬
scene: 矿区的老照片挂在会议室墙上，一边是装满矿石的卡车，一边是被挖空的山体。 The company's exploitation of the local iron ore lasted forty years.
sceneCN: 这里指对自然资源的开采利用（第 1 个义项：资源开发利用）；句意为这家公司对当地铁矿的开发持续了四十年。图中可辨识物件：露天矿坑、运矿卡车、山体剖面、会议室照片墙。

pos.zh: 开发利用；资源开采；剥削；利用

由动词加表示性质的形容词尾构成，义为「剥削性的」
由动词加表示「可……的」形容词尾构成，义为「可利用的」
由表示「过度」的前缀加本词构成，义为「过度开发」

senses.title: Productive use of natural resources
senses.definition: the working of land, minerals, water or forests for economic benefit
senses.definitionCN: 对土地、矿产、水源或森林进行有经济收益的开发利用
senses.example: The company's exploitation of the local iron ore lasted forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司对当地铁矿的开发持续了四十年。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a deed carried out and brought to profit, so working a mine counts as an exploit before it counts as abuse.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是「做成一件事并从中获利」，因此开采矿山先被算作一番作为，之后才被算作剥削。

senses.title: Commercial development of an idea or market
senses.definition: the turning of an invention, brand or market into a source of revenue
senses.definitionCN: 把发明、品牌或市场变成收入来源
senses.example: Critics said the film was a commercial exploitation of a true story.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说这部电影是对一个真实故事的商业开发。
senses.why: When the resource is an idea or a market rather than a mine, the same word means packaging it for sale.
senses.whyCN: 当被开发的对象从矿山变成创意或市场，同一个词就指把它包装出售。

senses.title: Use of data or personal information
senses.titleCN: 数据与个人信息的利用
senses.definition: the collection and use of data, often without the clear consent of the people concerned
senses.definitionCN: 收集并使用数据，且常常没有获得当事人的明确同意
senses.example: The inquiry examined the exploitation of user data by the platform.
senses.exampleCN: 调查审查了该平台对用户数据的使用。
senses.why: Data became a resource in the digital economy, and the word followed the resource.
senses.whyCN: 在数字经济中数据成了资源，这个词也就跟着资源走。

senses.title: Unfair use of labour
senses.definition: the payment of very little for long or hard work while another party keeps the profit
senses.definitionCN: 以极低报酬换取长时间或高强度劳动，利润归他方所有
senses.example: Inspectors found exploitation of migrant workers on the construction site.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员发现工地上存在对移民工人的剥削。
senses.why: Here the thing being worked is a person, and the profit is taken from their hours and body.
senses.whyCN: 这里被「开发」的对象是人，利润取自他们的工时与身体。

senses.title: Taking advantage of generosity
senses.definition: the use of someone's kindness, trust or weakness for one's own benefit
senses.definitionCN: 利用他人的善意、信任或弱点为自己谋利
senses.example: He described the loan as an exploitation of his father's generosity.
senses.exampleCN: 他把这笔借款说成是对父亲善意的利用。
senses.why: No mine and no market are needed: a human weakness is the seam being excavated.
senses.whyCN: 既不需要矿山也不需要市场：被开采的矿脉是人的弱点。

senses.title: Abuse of a vulnerable group
senses.definition: a systematic taking of value from people who cannot refuse, such as children or the poor
senses.definitionCN: 从无法拒绝的人身上系统性地榨取价值，如儿童或穷人
senses.example: The report documented exploitation of children in the informal economy.
senses.exampleCN: 报告记录了大量非正规经济中对儿童的剥削。
senses.why: The word turns from individual meanness to a structure when the group itself has no power to say no.
senses.whyCN: 当整个群体没有拒绝的能力时，这个词就从个人的刻薄变成一种结构。

senses.title: Extraction beyond renewal
senses.titleCN: 超出再生能力的过度攫取
senses.definition: harvesting or extraction at a rate faster than a natural system can recover
senses.definitionCN: 采伐或捕捞的速度快过自然系统的恢复能力
senses.example: Over-exploitation of the fishery left the boats with empty nets.
senses.exampleCN: 对渔场的过度捕捞让渔船空手而归。
senses.why: The prefix of excess turns the same act into one that destroys its own resource.
senses.whyCN: 表示「过度」的前缀把同一行为变成毁掉自身资源的行为。

senses.title: Use of a technical flaw
senses.definition: the deliberate use of a weakness in software or a system to gain access or control
senses.definitionCN: 故意利用软件或系统中的弱点取得访问权或控制权
senses.example: The attack began with exploitation of an unpatched browser flaw.
senses.exampleCN: 这次攻击始于对一个未修补的浏览器漏洞的利用。
senses.why: A loophole is a resource too: security language borrowed the word for a hole opened on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 漏洞也是一种资源：安全领域借用了这个词，指一个被故意打开的缺口。

senses.title: Full use of an opportunity
senses.definition: the energetic use of a chance or advantage that is legitimately available
senses.definitionCN: 对一个正当可用的机会或优势加以充分利用
senses.example: The coach praised the team's exploitation of every scoring chance.
senses.exampleCN: 教练称赞球队充分利用了每一次得分机会。
senses.why: The neutral sense survives in sport and business, where using an opening well is simply good play.
senses.whyCN: 这个中性含义在体育与商业中留存：把空档用好，本身就是好球。

intro.en: Exploitation goes back to a Latin verb meaning to unfold, through French a deed or a profit, and then to the modern sense of working a resource.
intro.cn: 这个词可追到拉丁语表示「展开」的动词，经法语表示「作为、获利」，再到现代「开发资源」的含义。

items.en: plicare meant to fold, and its compounds describe bending something into layers.
items.cn: plicare 意为「折叠」，其复合词描述把某物折成层。

items.en: ex- plus plicare gave explicare, to unfold or set out in order.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的前缀加「折叠」，构成 explicare，意为「展开、摊开说明」。

items.en: The participle explicitum named something unfolded and therefore made clear.
items.cn: 分词形式 explicitum 指被展开、因而变得清楚的事物。

items.en: French turned the idea into esploit, a deed accomplished, and later a source of profit.
items.cn: 法语把这一意思变成 esploit，指做成的一番作为，后来指利润来源。

items.en: English first used the deed word as exploit and built exploitation on it; the first records cluster in the early modern period and the exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语先把「作为」这个词用作 exploit，再由此构成 exploitation；首见记录集中出现在近代早期，具体年份不确定。

items.en: Industrial mining and factory labour gave the noun its double life as resource development and human abuse.
items.cn: 工业化采矿与工厂劳动让这个名词有了双面人生：资源开发与对人的剥削。

note.en: The first group shares form or root with exploitation; the second group names nearby ideas of using something for gain.
note.cn: 第一组在形音或词根上与 exploitation 相近；第二组是与「为获利而使用」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: A person or firm that works a resource or takes advantage of others.
entries.definitionCN: 指开发资源的个人或企业，或占他人便宜的人。

entries.definition: Describing a relationship or practice that extracts value unfairly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容不公平榨取价值的关系或做法。

entries.definition: The search for resources or knowledge; it looks close but comes from a verb meaning to search out, not to unfold.
entries.definitionCN: 指对资源或知识的勘探与探索；形近，但来自表示「搜寻」而非「展开」的动词。

entries.definition: Stated fully and leaving nothing folded away; it shares the unfolding image.
entries.definitionCN: 指表述完整、毫不含糊；与本词共享「展开」的意象。

entries.definition: The process of bringing land, resources or ideas into productive use; neutral and often positive.
entries.definitionCN: 指把土地、资源或想法带入生产用途的过程；中性且常为正面。

entries.definition: The effective use of something available; it stresses use, not profit or harm.
entries.definitionCN: 指对可用之物的有效使用；强调使用，不强调获利或伤害。

entries.definition: The wrong or harmful use of a power, substance or person; it stresses harm rather than extraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指对权力、物质或人的错误有害使用；强调伤害而非榨取。

entries.definition: Taking plants, fish or animals faster than they can replenish; the ecological twin of over-exploitation.
entries.definitionCN: 指对植物、鱼或动物的捕捞采集快于其补充；是「过度开发」的生态学说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin image of unfolding, the real French deed word and the real resource-and-labour pairs.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「展开」意象、真实的法语「作为」词，以及真实的资源与劳动搭配。

normal.en: The root picture is unfolding: a mine is land unfolded and spread out for profit.
normal.cn: 词根的意象是「展开」：矿山就是被摊开来换钱的土地。

normal.en: French esploit meant a deed done; exploitation is that deed turned into a business.
normal.cn: 法语 esploit 指做成一件事；exploitation 就是这件作为变成了生意。

normal.en: The same word covers a mine and a worker because both are seams someone works.
normal.cn: 同一个词既指矿山又指工人，因为两者都是被人开采的矿脉。

normal.en: Resource exploitation and labour exploitation sit on one page of the dictionary.
normal.cn: 资源开发与劳动剥削在词典的同一页上。

normal.en: Data is the new seam: data exploitation repeats the mining image.
normal.cn: 数据是新的矿脉：数据利用重复了采矿的意象。

abstract.en: Exploitation begins when a thing with its own life is seen only as something to be taken from.
abstract.cn: 剥削始于把一个有自己的生命的东西，只看成可供取用之物。

abstract.en: The word is neutral until the second party cannot say no; then development becomes extraction.
abstract.cn: 这个词本中性，直到另一方无法说不，开发就变成了榨取。

abstract.en: Every loophole is a small hole opened on purpose, which is why security borrowed the mining word.
abstract.cn: 每一个漏洞都是一个被故意打开的小口，所以安全领域借用了采矿的词。

examples.en: The treaty set limits on the exploitation of the river for hydropower.
examples.cn: 该条约对这条河的水电开发设定了限制。

examples.en: The court treated the long unpaid internships as exploitation of young workers.
examples.cn: 法院把长期无薪实习视为对年轻劳动者的剥削。

examples.en: Security teams patched the flaw before exploitation of it became widespread.
examples.cn: 安全团队在漏洞被广泛利用之前就完成了修补。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「爱克斯普洛伊泰申」——把矿藏「展开」摊开，再从中取利

root: 来自拉丁语 explicare「展开、摊开说明」← ex-「向外」+ plicare「折叠」，分词 explicitum 指「展开的」；经古法语 esploit「作为、获利」与法语 exploiter 进入英语，再由动词构成 exploitation。首见年代为约数，来源链清楚。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from working a mine, a market, data and a person to passing the limit and to two neutral uses in security and sport.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从开采矿山、开发市场、利用数据和剥削人，走到越过限度，最后落到安全与体育里两个中性用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hillside is unfolded layer by layer, ore goes one way and people stay at the pit edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：山坡被一层层展开，矿石被运走，人留在矿坑边缘。

branches.en: THE LAND AND THE MARKET: ore, land and ideas turned into revenue.
branches.cn: 土地与市场：矿石、土地与创意被换成收入。

branches.en: THE DATA SEAM: records mined for value, often without consent.
branches.cn: 数据矿脉：记录被开采出价值，常常未经同意。

branches.en: THE PERSON AS RESOURCE: hours, kindness and weakness turned into another's gain.
branches.cn: 把人当资源：工时、善意与弱点变成他人的收益。

branches.en: THE LIMIT PASSED: harvest that outruns renewal and destroys the seam.
branches.cn: 越过限度：收割快过再生，最终毁掉矿脉本身。

branches.en: THE OPEN HOLE: a system flaw or a brief chance used to the full.
branches.cn: 敞开的缺口：系统漏洞或短暂机会被充分利用。

intro.en: Exploitation is a verb stem plus a noun ending, with a Latin prefix and a Latin root still visible inside.
intro.cn: 这个词是动词词干加名词词尾，内部仍能看见一个拉丁前缀与一个拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies plicare and explicare, and the participle explicitum; French supplies the deed word exploit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 plicare、explicare 与分词 explicitum；法语提供了表示「作为」的 exploit。

items.example: It marks the unfolding outward.
items.exampleCN: 它标记「向外展开」。

items.example: The root names folded layers.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名折叠的层。

items.example: Prefix and root combine into the key verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与词根合成关键动词。

items.example: The participle supplies the clear sense.
items.exampleCN: 分词提供了「清楚」的含义。

items.example: It forms the English action noun.
items.exampleCN: 它构成英语的动作名词。

items.meaning: to work for gain; a bold deed
items.example: The base word keeps both sides.
items.exampleCN: 基础词兼含两面。

items.example: It forms exploiter, the one who works the seam.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 exploiter，指开采矿脉的人。

items.example: It forms exploitative, the unfair kind.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 exploitative，指剥削性的。

items.example: It forms exploitable, able to be used.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 exploitable，指可利用的。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加施动者词尾构成，义为「开发者；剥削者」
由动词加性质形容词尾构成，义为「剥削性的」
由动词加「可……的」形容词尾构成，义为「可利用的」
由「过度」前缀加本词构成，义为「过度开发」

definition_zh: 剥削性的；利用性的；掠夺性的；猎奇的
definition_en: treating other people or natural resources unfairly in order to gain money or an advantage
core_image: 一个人被压在磨盘下，上面的人还不断往磨盘上添石头
scene: 那家工厂让工人一天干十几个小时，却只给很少的工钱。The factory is widely criticised as exploitative because it pays so little for such long hours.
sceneCN: 这里 exploitative 是「剥削性的」（第 1 个义项：以不公平的条件榨取他人的劳动）；句意：这家工厂工时长而工钱少，被广泛批评为剥削性的企业。

pos.zh: 剥削性的；利用性的；掠夺性的；猎奇的

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「剥削；利用；开发」，形容词即由它加 -ative 构成
由 exploit 加 -ation 构成，义为「剥削；利用；开发」
由 exploit 加 -er 构成，义为「剥削者」
exploitative 的异体形式，义为「剥削性的」，使用频率较低

senses.title: Taking unfair profit from labour
senses.definition: making money from the work of other people while giving them too little in return
senses.definitionCN: 靠他人的劳动赚钱，却只给出过少的回报
senses.example: The garment factory was attacked for its exploitative wages.
senses.exampleCN: 这家制衣厂因剥削性工资而受到抨击。
senses.why: The Latin root names unfolding a gain, and the adjective keeps the sense of turning the effort of other people into profit.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根意为「把收益展开」，这个形容词保留了「把别人的付出变成自己的利润」这一层意思。

senses.title: Using a person for your own ends
senses.definition: treating a person as a means to your own advantage, especially in a close relationship
senses.definitionCN: 把人当作达到自己好处的手段，尤指在亲密关系中
senses.example: She described the friendship as exploitative and stopped seeing him.
senses.exampleCN: 她说这段友谊是在利用她，于是不再见他。
senses.why: Once profit is no longer about money, the same word covers emotional and personal advantage.
senses.whyCN: 当「利润」不再限于金钱，同一个词就扩展到情感与人际层面的好处。

senses.title: Taking too much from nature
senses.definition: taking resources from the land or the sea faster than they can renew
senses.definitionCN: 从陆地或海洋取用资源的速度超过其再生速度
senses.example: Exploitative logging has stripped the hillside bare.
senses.exampleCN: 掠夺性伐木把山坡砍得光秃秃的。
senses.why: Resources can be exploited like workers, so the adjective moves easily from people to land and water.
senses.whyCN: 资源可以像工人一样被榨取，所以这个形容词从人扩展到土地与水域并不费力。

senses.title: Profiting from private suffering
senses.definition: using the suffering or private life of other people to attract attention and sell stories
senses.definitionCN: 利用他人的痛苦或私生活来吸引注意力、推销内容
senses.example: Critics called the documentary exploitative rather than sympathetic.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家说这部纪录片是在消费他人，而非出于同情。
senses.why: Media profit comes from attention, so the same adjective now describes stories that turn pain into traffic.
senses.whyCN: 媒体的利润来自注意力，于是这个形容词又用来描述把痛苦换成流量的报道。

intro.en: Exploitative comes from exploit, which English took from Old French esploit, a deed or a profit, and which goes back to Latin explicare, to unfold.
intro.cn: exploitative 来自 exploit，英语从古法语 esploit（功业、收益）借入，而它更早可追到拉丁语 explicare（展开）。

items.en: Plicare means to fold, and ex- means out, so explicare is to unfold.
items.cn: plicare 意为折叠，ex- 意为向外，因此 explicare 是「展开」。

items.en: Explicitum, the folded-out thing, comes to mean what is accomplished or achieved.
items.cn: explicitum 指「被展开的东西」，引申为已完成、已取得的成果。

items.en: Esploit means a deed, an achievement, or a profit.
items.cn: esploit 意为功业、成就或收益。

items.en: English exploit first names a bold deed, then the profit taken from work.
items.cn: 英语 exploit 先指英勇的事迹，后指从劳动中取得的收益。

items.en: The adjective exploitative spreads with the growth of criticism of industrial labour.
items.cn: 随着对工业劳动的批评兴起，形容词 exploitative 逐渐流传开来。

items.en: Modern English applies it to labour, relationships, resources, and media.
items.cn: 现代英语把它用于劳动、人际关系、资源与媒体。

note.en: Exploitative sits in the exploit family, and it shares ground with words for unfair advantage.
note.cn: exploitative 属于 exploit 词族，并与一批表示「不公平占便宜」的词在语义上重叠。

entries.definition: to use someone or something for gain
the act of using people or resources for gain
a less common variant of exploitative
entries.definitionCN: exploitative 的异体形式，只是拼写不同

entries.definition: treating people in a cruel and unfair way
taking advantage of others for your own gain
not just or equal

normalIntro.en: Exploitative is exploit plus -ative: it describes anyone who turns the effort of other people into profit.
normalIntro.cn: exploitative 是 exploit 加 -ative：它形容那些把别人的付出变成自己利润的人或做法。

normal.en: An exploitative employer takes more than the work is worth.
normal.cn: 剥削成性的雇主拿走的东西超过劳动本身的价值。

normal.en: An exploitative relationship leaves one person tired and the other comfortable.
normal.cn: 利用性的关系让一方疲惫，另一方舒服。

normal.en: Exploitative fishing empties the sea faster than fish can breed.
normal.cn: 掠夺性捕捞让海里的鱼来不及繁殖就被捞空。

normal.en: The noun is exploitation, and the person who does it is an exploiter.
normal.cn: 名词是 exploitation，实施者叫 exploiter。

normal.en: Compare exploitative with hard: hard work is demanding, exploitative work is unfair.
normal.cn: 对比 exploitative 与 hard：hard 只说明活儿累，exploitative 说明条件不公。

abstract.en: Picture a millstone pressing down while someone above keeps adding weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一块磨盘压下来，上面的人还不断加重量。

abstract.en: Think of a hand squeezing a fruit until nothing is left in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把果子攥到一滴汁都不剩。

abstract.en: Picture a net so fine that even the smallest fish cannot slip through.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网眼细到连最小的鱼都钻不出去的网。

examples.en: Campaigners say the pay system is exploitative and want it changed.
examples.cn: 活动人士说这套薪酬制度是剥削性的，要求加以改变。

examples.en: The novel shows an exploitative marriage that slowly drains both people.
examples.cn: 这部小说写了一段慢慢耗干两个人的利用性婚姻。

examples.en: Exploitative tourism damages the very places it sells.
examples.cn: 掠夺性旅游损害的正是它所推销的那些地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「exploit + ative」——把「利用」加上形容词尾巴，就成了「剥削性的」；谐音可记成「一克斯普洛伊特提夫」，纯属联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）+ plicare（折叠）→ explicare（展开）→ 拉丁语 explicitum（已完成的事）→ 古法语 esploit（功业、收益）→ 英语 exploit → 加 -ative 构成 exploitative，核心义是「把他人的东西展开、收进自己囊中」。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective starts from unfair profit taken from labour, widens to personal and emotional use, then to resources, and finally to media that sell private pain.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词从榨取劳动的不公平利润出发，扩展到人际与情感上的利用，再到对自然资源的掠夺，最后落到靠贩卖他人痛苦获利的媒体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a millstone that grows heavier every time the person below tries to stand.
core.cn: 核心意象：磨盘在下面的人每次想站起来时都变得更重。

branches.en: Profit taken from labour is the economic core of the word.
branches.cn: 从劳动中取利，是这个词的经济核心。

branches.en: Emotional advantage is the personal version of the same pattern.
branches.cn: 情感上的好处，是同一模式的私人版本。

branches.en: Nature can be drained just as workers can be worked out.
branches.cn: 自然可以被抽干，正如工人可以被用尽。

branches.en: Attention is also a currency, so private pain becomes a product.
branches.cn: 注意力也是一种货币，于是私人的痛苦成了产品。

branches.en: Both underpaid labour and profitable suffering turn a person into a means.
branches.cn: 低薪劳动与有利可图的苦难，都把一个人变成了手段。

intro.en: Exploitative combines the verb exploit with the suffix -ative, and the family runs through exploit, exploitation, and exploiter.
intro.cn: exploitative 由动词 exploit 加词尾 -ative 构成，同族词包括 exploit、exploitation 与 exploiter。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb explicare, to unfold, lies behind the French esploit that English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 explicare（展开）是英语借入的法语 esploit 的更早来源。

items.example: The prefix ex- opens the image of unfolding.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 打开了「展开」这一意象。

items.example: Plicare supplies the folded image.
items.exampleCN: plicare 提供「折叠」的意象。

items.example: Explicare joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: explicare 把前缀与词根合起来。

items.example: Esploit is the French form English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: esploit 是英语借入的法语形式。

items.meaning: to use someone or something for gain
items.example: To exploit a worker is to take more than you give.
items.exampleCN: 剥削一个工人，就是拿走的比给的多。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms exploitation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 exploitation。

items.meaning: the act of using people or resources for gain
items.example: Exploitation names the act behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: exploitation 为这个形容词提供行为名词。

items.meaning: tending to, having the nature of
items.example: The suffix -ative forms exploitative.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ative 构成 exploitative。

items.example: An exploiter takes the profit and leaves the risk.
items.exampleCN: 剥削者拿走利润，把风险留下。

definition_zh: 探索性的；勘探的；试探性的
definition_en: intended to search out, investigate or test something whose outcome is not yet known
core_image: 一个人举着火把走进尚未绘制的洞穴，边走边把路线记在纸上
scene: 这里指「探索性的」。 The team ran an exploratory survey before committing money to the full excavation.
sceneCN: 这里 exploratory 是「探索性的、摸底性质的」（第 1 个义项：为了先弄清情况而做的调查）；句意：团队在投入全部开挖资金之前先做了一次探索性勘测。图中可辨识物件：火把、洞穴入口、测绘图、标记桩。

pos.zh: 探索性的；勘探的；试探性的

derivatives.zh: 探索性的（与 exploratory 近义，更少用）

senses.title: Searching out the unknown
senses.definition: done in order to find out what exists or what is happening, before any final decision is made
senses.definitionCN: 为了先弄清存在什么、正在发生什么而做的，尚未作出最终决定
senses.example: An exploratory visit to the site revealed two problems the report had missed.
senses.exampleCN: 对现场的一次探索性走访发现了报告漏掉的两个问题。
senses.why: explorare in Latin means 'to search out'. The -ory suffix marks a purpose, so an exploratory action exists for the sake of searching, not for the sake of a result.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 explorare 意为“搜出、查明”。-ory 后缀标记用途，所以 exploratory 的行为是为“查”本身而存在，不是为某个既定结果服务。

senses.title: Probing the ground
senses.titleCN: 勘探的：先打孔看看地下
senses.definition: relating to the search for oil, minerals or water under the ground
senses.definitionCN: 与寻找地下石油、矿产或水有关的
senses.example: Exploratory wells are cheap compared with the wells that actually produce oil.
senses.exampleCN: 与真正出油的井相比，勘探井的成本很低。
senses.why: Mining and oil use the same word because the search happens before extraction. The hole is a question, not yet an answer.
senses.whyCN: 采矿与石油业沿用同一个词，因为“找”发生在“采”之前。那个钻孔是一个问题，还不是答案。

senses.title: Tentative, not final
senses.titleCN: 试探性的：先走一步看反应
senses.definition: acting as a first cautious step whose results will decide whether to continue
senses.definitionCN: 作为谨慎的第一步、由结果决定是否继续的
senses.example: The company sent an exploratory email rather than a formal offer.
senses.exampleCN: 公司发了一封试探性的邮件，而不是正式报价。
senses.why: A tentative step keeps the door open. The word borrows the miner's caution: you test the ground before you build on it.
senses.whyCN: 试探性的一步保留了退路。这个词借用了矿工的谨慎：先试地下，再在上面动工。

senses.title: Medical probing
senses.titleCN: 探查性的：打开看看里面怎么了
senses.definition: describing surgery or a clinical trial carried out to find the cause or the safe dose
senses.definitionCN: 指为查明病因或安全剂量而进行的手术或临床试验
senses.example: Exploratory surgery showed that the pain came from a small adhesion.
senses.exampleCN: 探查性手术显示疼痛来自一处小的粘连。
senses.why: Medicine borrows the mining image directly: the body is opened to look, because scans have not explained enough.
senses.whyCN: 医学直接借用了采矿的意象：扫描没能解释清楚，于是打开身体去看。

senses.title: Learning by discovery
senses.titleCN: 探索式学习的：让学生自己找到答案
senses.definition: describing teaching in which learners investigate a question instead of receiving the answer
senses.definitionCN: 指让学习者自行探究问题、而不是直接接受答案的教学方式
senses.example: The exploratory lesson began with a question and no textbook page.
senses.exampleCN: 这堂探索式课程从一个问题开始，没有对应的课本页。
senses.why: Here the search moves inside the classroom: the student repeats the original act of finding out, and the finding is the lesson.
senses.whyCN: 这里“找”移到了教室内部：学生重复了最初那个“查明”的动作，而查到的过程本身就是课。

senses.title: Statistics: open-ended analysis
senses.titleCN: 探索性数据分析的：先看数据长什么样
senses.definition: in statistics, describing analysis that looks for patterns before a specific hypothesis is fixed
senses.definitionCN: 统计学上指在确定假设之前先寻找数据模式的分析
senses.example: Exploratory analysis found a cluster of outliers in the northern stations.
senses.exampleCN: 探索性分析在北部站点发现了一簇离群值。
senses.why: Exploratory data analysis reverses the usual order: instead of testing a guess, it lets the data suggest the guess, which is again a search outward.
senses.whyCN: 探索性数据分析颠倒了通常顺序：不是检验某个猜想，而是让数据提出猜想，仍然是向外搜找。

senses.title: First-round talks
senses.titleCN: 探索性会谈：先摸摸对方底线
senses.definition: describing early discussions whose purpose is to discover whether agreement is possible
senses.definitionCN: 指目的在于探明能否达成协议的早期磋商
senses.example: Exploratory talks resumed in Geneva after a three-month pause.
senses.exampleCN: 探索性会谈在中断三个月后于日内瓦重启。
senses.why: Diplomacy uses exploratory for talks that are not yet negotiations. Nothing is conceded; the only product is information.
senses.whyCN: 外交上用 exploratory 指还算不上谈判的会谈：不作让步，唯一的产出是信息。

senses.title: Testing the environment
senses.titleCN: 试探行为的：伸出一只脚试试水深
senses.definition: in animal and human behaviour, describing actions that gather information about a new setting
senses.definitionCN: 在动物与人类行为研究中，指为获取新环境信息而做的动作
senses.example: Exploratory behaviour in the young rats increased when the cage was new.
senses.exampleCN: 笼子换成新的时，幼鼠的探索行为增加了。
senses.why: Behavioural science keeps the physical image: an organism reaches out, touches, retreats, and maps the space by movement.
senses.whyCN: 行为科学保留了身体意象：生物伸手、触碰、退回，用移动把空间画成地图。

intro.en: Exploratory comes from Latin explorare 'to search out, investigate', built on ex- 'out' plus plorare 'to cry out'. The image is a hunter shouting while searching. English added -ory to make the adjective.
intro.cn: exploratory 来自拉丁语 explorare“搜出、调查”，由 ex-“向外”加 plorare“呼喊”构成。意象是猎人在搜寻时大声呼喊。英语加上 -ory 构成形容词。

items.en: plorare meant 'to cry out, wail'. Its further origin is uncertain; some scholars connect it with pluere 'to rain', but this is a guess and should be marked source uncertain.
items.cn: plorare 意为“大声喊、哭喊”。其更深来源不确定，有学者把它与 pluere“下雨”联系起来，但这只是推测，应标注“来源不确定”。

items.en: ex- 'out' plus plorare produced explorare, 'to cry out while searching', hence 'to search out, examine'. The shout is the signal that someone is looking.
items.cn: ex-“向外”加 plorare 构成 explorare，意为“一边搜寻一边呼喊”，引申为“搜出、检查”。喊声就是“有人在找”的信号。

items.en: explorator was a scout or spy, the person who went ahead to see what was there. The noun keeps the human agent of the search.
items.cn: explorator 是侦察兵、探子，先行去看情况的人。这个名词保留了“搜寻”的执行者。

items.en: English builds exploratory on the stem explorat- plus -ory, from Latin -orius 'serving for'. The adjective appears in the 17th century, first in religious and then in scientific writing.
items.cn: 英语以 explorat- 词干加 -ory（来自拉丁 -orius“用于……”）构成 exploratory。该形容词出现于 17 世纪，最早见于宗教写作，随后进入科学写作。

items.en: From the 19th century exploratory spreads to surgery, drilling and field surveys, where the search must happen before any commitment.
items.cn: 19 世纪起，exploratory 扩展到外科、钻探与野外勘测，这些场合都必须先搜寻、后投入。

items.en: In the 20th century the word reaches statistics and diplomacy, naming analysis and talks that deliberately avoid a fixed conclusion.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词进入统计学与外交领域，指刻意不预设结论的分析与会谈。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ex- or -plor- shape but not always the same root; the near-meaning group shares the idea of a first, cautious step.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ex- 或 -plor- 的外形，但未必同根；近义组都含“先走一步、谨慎试探”的意思。

entries.definition: another adjective from the same verb, meaning 'tending to explore'. It describes a quality, while exploratory describes a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词派生的另一形容词，意为“有探索倾向的”。它描述性质，而 exploratory 描述用途。

entries.definition: the act of searching or travelling to find out. The noun names the activity; the adjective names what the activity is for.
entries.definitionCN: 探索、勘探的行为。名词命名活动本身；形容词命名活动的用途。

entries.definition: taking unfair advantage of people or resources. It looks close because of ex- and -or-, but exploit comes from Latin explicare 'unfold', not from plorare.
entries.definitionCN: 剥削性的；利用他人或资源的。它因 ex- 与 -or- 而形近，但 exploit 来自拉丁 explicare“展开”，并非 plorare。

entries.definition: concerned with discovering facts, often formally. It stresses method and evidence, while exploratory stresses the open, unfinished stage.
entries.definitionCN: 调查性的；重在查明事实，常带正式色彩。它强调方法与证据，而 exploratory 强调开放、未定型的阶段。

entries.definition: coming before the main part as preparation. It marks order, not necessarily search.
entries.definitionCN: 初步的；作为主要部分之前的准备。它标记顺序，不一定含“搜寻”之意。

entries.definition: done or said in a cautious way, ready to be changed. It describes hesitation, while exploratory describes the information being sought.
entries.definitionCN: 试探性的；谨慎且可更改的。它描述犹豫，而 exploratory 描述被搜寻的信息。

entries.definition: used as an adjective for a small trial that tests whether a larger plan will work. It is close to exploratory but implies a planned full version to follow.
entries.definitionCN: 试点性的；以小规模试验检验更大计划是否可行。它接近 exploratory，但暗含之后有计划的完整版本。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + plorare 'cry out': the explorer is the one who shouts outward while looking.
normal.cn: ex-“向外”+ plorare“呼喊”：探索者就是一边向外喊、一边找的人。

normal.en: exploration, explore and explorer all keep the same stem, so the family is learned as one block.
normal.cn: exploration、explore、explorer 共享同一词干，可以整块记忆。

normal.en: exploratory talks and exploratory drilling are both first steps that produce information, not final products.
normal.cn: exploratory talks 与 exploratory drilling 都是产出信息、不产出成品的第一步。

normal.en: exploratory surgery is literally opening the body to look, which is the clearest picture of the word.
normal.cn: exploratory surgery 字面上就是打开身体去看，是这个词最清楚的画面。

normal.en: The opposite situation is a confirmatory study, which tests a claim already fixed; exploratory looks before the claim exists.
normal.cn: 反面的情形是 confirmatory study（确证性研究），检验已经固定的主张；exploratory 则是在主张出现之前先看。

abstract.en: Think of a lantern sweeping across a cave wall: the beam does not build anything, it only shows what is there.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯扫过洞壁：光束不建造任何东西，只是把已有的东西照出来。

abstract.en: Think of a hand testing the temperature of water with one finger before the whole body enters.
abstract.cn: 想象先用一根手指试水温，然后整个身体才下水。

abstract.en: Think of a map that is still mostly blank, with a dotted line marking where someone has already walked.
abstract.cn: 想象一张大半空白的地图，只有一条虚线标出已经走过的路。

examples.en: The ministry funded an exploratory project to see whether the soil could hold a dam.
examples.cn: 该部门资助了一个探索性项目，看看这土壤能否承住一座水坝。

examples.en: After two exploratory meetings, both sides agreed to draft a real treaty.
examples.cn: 经过两次探索性会谈，双方同意起草一份正式条约。

examples.en: Exploratory analysis is useful precisely because it does not decide the answer in advance.
examples.cn: 探索性分析之所以有用，恰恰因为它不预先决定答案。

dict_mnemonic.text: “往外铺路”——ex（向外）+ plor（铺路的“铺”音近）：先向外铺一条小路，边走边看 → exploratory 探索性的

root: 拉丁 explorare“搜出、调查”（ex-“向外”+ plorare“呼喊”，plorare 的更深来源不确定）；explorat- 词干 + -ory“用于……的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one motion: a person moves outward into unmapped ground, and the moving itself is the point.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个动作：人向外走进尚未绘图的地方，而“走”本身就是目的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lantern moving into an unmapped cave.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯移进尚未绘图的洞穴。

branches.en: SEARCH AND SURVEY: the general search and the miner's test hole are the same outward movement, one on land and one under it.
branches.cn: 搜寻与勘测：一般性探索与矿工的试孔是同一个向外动作，一个在地面，一个在地下。

branches.en: CAUTIOUS FIRST STEP: an exploratory email and exploratory talks both buy information before commitment.
branches.cn: 谨慎的第一步：试探性邮件与探索性会谈，都在投入之前先换取信息。

branches.en: MEDICAL PROBE: surgery that opens the body to look is the literal version of the same search.
branches.cn: 医学探查：为看清楚而打开身体的手术，是同一搜寻的字面版本。

branches.en: LEARNING: discovery-based teaching moves the search inside the learner, who repeats the original act.
branches.cn: 学习：发现式教学把搜寻移进学习者内部，让他重复最初的动作。

branches.en: OPEN-ENDED INQUIRY: data analysis and animal exploration both gather patterns before any hypothesis is fixed.
branches.cn: 开放式探究：数据分析与动物探索都在固定假设之前先收集模式。

intro.en: Exploratory is a Latin stem with the English suffix -ory. The ex- prefix is still readable as 'out', while -ory marks purpose; -tion and -er build the noun family.
intro.cn: exploratory 是拉丁词干加英语后缀 -ory。ex- 前缀仍可读作“向外”，-ory 标记用途；-tion 与 -er 构成名词族。

latinIntro.en: The family grows from plorare 'cry out' through explorare 'search out' to explorator 'scout'. The stem appears as explor- in English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族从 plorare“呼喊”经 explorare“搜出”生长到 explorator“侦察者”。英语中词干作 explor-。

items.exampleCN: 他们花了三天探索那个洞穴。

items.meaningCN: 探索者；探险家（-er 构成施事名词）

items.example: Much of the cave remains unexplored.

items.meaningCN: 以探索的方式（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: She asked the question exploratively rather than as a challenge.

senses.title: Travel to learn
senses.definition: to travel through a place to learn about it
senses.definitionCN: 穿行某地以了解它
senses.example: They explored the cave by torchlight.
senses.exampleCN: 他们借着火把的光探索洞穴。
senses.why: The core sense is searching a new place.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是搜寻新地方。

senses.title: Examine an idea
senses.definition: to examine an idea or subject carefully
senses.definitionCN: 仔细考察一个想法或主题
senses.example: The book explores the causes of war.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书探讨战争的起因。

definition_zh: 探险家；探索者；勘探者；浏览器
definition_en: a person who travels through unknown places to find out what is there, or a program that lets a user browse files or web pages
core_image: 背着行囊，跨过地图上最后一条线的人
scene: 地图边缘还是一片空白，他却已经把行囊背上了肩。The explorer set out for the blank space at the edge of the map.

senses.title: A traveller of unknown land
senses.definition: a person who goes into an unknown region in order to find out what is there
senses.definitionCN: 进入未知地域以了解当地情况的人
senses.example: The explorer spent four months crossing the ice.
senses.exampleCN: 这位探险家花了四个月穿越冰原。
senses.why: The Latin verb behind the word means to search out, and the -er ending marks the person who does the searching.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁语动词意为「搜寻出来」，后缀 -er 又标出做这件事的人，于是「往外搜寻的人」就是探险家。

senses.title: A person who searches out an idea
senses.definition: a person who studies an unfamiliar subject or idea in depth
senses.definitionCN: 深入研究陌生课题或想法的人
senses.example: She is an explorer of how children learn language.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位研究儿童如何学习语言的探索者。
senses.why: Searching out applies to ideas as well as coasts, so the same word covers people who chart thought instead of land.
senses.whyCN: 「搜寻出来」既可用于土地，也可用于想法，所以同一个词也指梳理思想而不是海岸线的人。

senses.title: A program for browsing
senses.definition: a computer program, often one named Explorer, that lets a user move through files or web pages
senses.definitionCN: 一种让用户在文件或网页之间移动的计算机程序，常以 Explorer 为名
senses.example: Open the file explorer to find the missing folder.
senses.exampleCN: 打开文件浏览器，找到那个不见了的文件夹。
senses.why: Browsing is a search made with the eyes, so the old word for a traveller was borrowed for software that walks a user through data.
senses.whyCN: 浏览是用眼睛做的搜寻，于是这个古老的「旅行者」词被借去指那种带用户在数据中行走的软件。

senses.title: A prospector or survey party
senses.definition: a person or company that searches an area for oil, minerals, or other resources
senses.definitionCN: 在一片区域里寻找石油、矿物或其他资源的人或公司
senses.example: The oil explorer drilled a test well near the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 这家石油勘探公司在三角洲附近打了一口探井。
senses.why: The act of searching a region for what lies hidden became the trade name for resource survey work.
senses.whyCN: 「在一片区域里搜寻隐藏之物」这一核心动作，后来成了资源勘查这一行的称呼。

note.en: Explorer belongs to the explore family and sits beside words for travellers and searchers.
note.cn: explorer 属于「探索」词族，与表示旅行者、先行者的词义场相邻。

entries.definition: to travel through a place in order to learn about it
the act of searching an unknown place
done in order to find out something
a person who looks for adventure
a person who is the first to open up a new field or region
a person sent ahead to gather information

normalIntro.en: Explorer is a search word: the -er ending marks the person who goes out and looks.
normalIntro.cn: explorer 是「搜寻」词：-er 结尾标出那个走出去查看的人。

normal.en: Explore is the verb and explorer is the person who does it.
normal.cn: explore 是动词，explorer 是做这件事的人。

normal.en: The ending -er turns an act into a role, as in teacher and writer.
normal.cn: 后缀 -er 把动作变成身份，teacher 与 writer 也是这么来的。

normal.en: Polar explorer and space explorer are common pairings.
normal.cn: 「polar explorer」与「space explorer」都是常见搭配。

normal.en: Exploration is the noun of the same family.
normal.cn: exploration 是同族的名称词。

normal.en: Compare browser: browser is the everyday word, and explorer survives mostly in product names.
normal.cn: 对比 browser：browser 是日常说法，explorer 多半留在产品名里。

abstract.en: Picture a flag planted where the map turns white.
abstract.cn: 想象在地图变白的地方插下一面旗。

abstract.en: Picture a reader tracing an unknown idea the way a hand traces a coastline.
abstract.cn: 想象读者像描海岸线一样描一个陌生的想法。

abstract.en: Picture a small window walking from folder to folder.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇小窗口在文件夹之间走来走去。

examples.en: The explorer reached the coast after a month on foot.
examples.cn: 这位探险家走了一个月才抵达海岸。

examples.en: Early explorers drew maps that were often wrong.
examples.cn: 早期的探险家画的地图常常是错的。

examples.en: Open the file explorer and search for the report.
examples.cn: 打开文件浏览器，搜索那份报告。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆音联想：ex 像「往外」，plorer 像「扑了」——一心往外扑向荒野的人，就是探险家；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）+ plorare（呼喊，一般认为源于狩猎时的出声）→ explorare（搜寻、勘察）→ explorator（侦察者）→ 古法语 explorer → 英语 explore + -er（做某事的人），核心义「向外搜寻的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Explorer starts as the person who searches out unknown land, extends to the person who searches out ideas, and then reaches software and the resource trade.
sensesIntro.cn: explorer 先是搜寻未知土地的人，再扩到梳理思想的人，最后落到软件窗口与资源勘查行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walker stepping past the last line drawn on the map.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个行者跨过地图上画出的最后一条线。

branches.en: The person who enters unknown land is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 进入未知土地的人，是最早的义项。

branches.en: The idea sense moves the search from ground to thought.
branches.cn: 涉及想法的义项把搜寻从土地移到了思想。

branches.en: The software sense borrows the walking image for data.
branches.cn: 软件义项把这幅行走的画面借给了数据。

branches.en: The resource sense narrows the search to what lies under the ground.
branches.cn: 资源义项把搜寻收窄到地下埋着的东西。

branches.en: The traveller and the survey party both go out to find what is not yet known.
branches.cn: 旅行者与勘查队都是走出去寻找尚未知道的东西。

intro.en: Explorer is built from Latin ex- and plorare, with explore, exploration, and exploratory around it.
intro.cn: explorer 由拉丁语 ex- 与 plorare 构成，周围有 explore、exploration 与 exploratory 同族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin explorare means to search out, and explorator means a scout.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 explorare 意为搜寻出来，explorator 意为侦察者。

items.example: The prefix ex- points the action outward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 把动作指向外面。

items.example: Plorare is said to be the hunter shout behind the word.
items.exampleCN: 一般认为 plorare 是这个词背后猎人的呼喊。

items.example: Explorare gives the searching core.
items.exampleCN: explorare 提供「搜寻」这一核心。

items.example: Explorator is the person sent ahead.
items.exampleCN: explorator 是先被派出去的人。

items.example: The suffix -er forms explorer from explore.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 由 explore 构成 explorer。

items.meaning: to search a place or subject
items.example: Explore is the short verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: explore 是这个词族的短动词。

items.example: Explorer keeps the person sense.
items.exampleCN: explorer 保留「人」的含义。

items.example: Exploration names the act rather than the person.
items.exampleCN: exploration 指行为，不指人。

items.example: Exploratory describes a first look.
items.exampleCN: exploratory 描述初次查看的性质。

items.example: Unexplored adds the negative prefix un-.
items.exampleCN: unexplored 加了否定前缀 un-。

senses.title: Able to explode
senses.definition: able or likely to explode

senses.example: The workers found an explosive device near the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们在桥附近发现了一枚爆炸装置。
senses.why: The core sense is the power to burst apart.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是具有炸裂的力量。

senses.title: Likely to erupt
senses.definition: likely to cause a sudden violent reaction or very fast growth
senses.definitionCN: 很可能引发突然的激烈反应或极快增长的
senses.example: The region saw explosive growth in tourism.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的旅游业出现了爆炸式增长。
senses.why: Physical bursting becomes sudden social change.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的炸开转为社会的骤然变化。

senses.title: An explosive substance
senses.definition: a substance that can explode
senses.definitionCN: 能够爆炸的物质
senses.example: The mine stores explosives in a secure shed.
senses.exampleCN: 矿场把炸药存放在安全的棚屋里。
senses.why: The quality becomes a physical material.
senses.whyCN: 性质变成一种具体的物质。

intro.en: Explosive belongs to the explode family, built on Latin ex- out and plaudere to clap.
